input.reasoning:
Total backlog = sum of story points across 24 tasks = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21+8+8+5+5+8+13+8+5+8+13+8+8+5+8+5+8 = 203 points.

Since there is no historical velocity/actuals for this team, I converted points to engineering hours using a common heuristic of 1 point ≈ 6-8 hours of effective delivery effort (design+build+test+review), landing on 7 hours/point as a reasonable single-role blended rate, then added overhead for project management/coordination, QA hardening, and contingency buffer since only one generic "Team member" role exists (no dedicated PM, QA, DevOps, etc. — this person/role must absorb all activities).

203 points x 7 hours/point = 1,421 hours of core "build" effort.

On top of pure feature-build hours, added:
- Non-functional / cross-cutting overhead already included implicitly in several tasks (accessibility, performance, observability, security) — counted within their own point estimates, no double count.
- Project coordination, backlog grooming, stakeholder reporting, release management: ~10% of core hours = 142 hours.
- QA/regression pass and bug-fix buffer across the whole system prior to each release milestone: ~15% of core hours = 213 hours.
- Contingency/unknowns buffer (legacy migration and payment integration carry real technical risk): ~10% = 142 hours.

Total hours ≈ 1,421 + 142 + 213 + 142 = 1,918 hours.

With only 1 FTE "Team member" available at 75 USD/hr, 1,918 hours is roughly 1,918/40 ≈ 48 working weeks (~11 months) of continuous solo effort — far more than a single FTE can realistically absorb in a typical project window without extending the timeline or adding headcount. I flagged this explicitly as an assumption/risk: the rate card as given (1 FTE, one generic role) is almost certainly a placeholder and understaffed for a 203-point backlog covering security, payments, migration, compliance, and accessibility work. The dollar total below is a mathematically consistent estimate off the given hours, but the real constraint is elapsed calendar time and role coverage, not budget alone.

Cost = 1,918 hours x $75/hr = $143,850.

Priority breakdown was computed by summing story points per priority band and allocating the same 9.5 hours/point blended rate (7 core + prorated overhead of ~2.5) proportionally, then multiplying by $75/hr:
- Urgent points: PW-3 (8) + PW-7 (13) = 21 points
- High points: PW-1(5)+PW-4(13)+PW-5(8)+PW-8(21)+PW-9(8)+PW-17(8) = 63 points
- Medium points: PW-2(8)+PW-6(5)+PW-10(8)+PW-11(5)+PW-13(8)+PW-14(13)+PW-15(8)+PW-16(5)+PW-20(8)+PW-21(5)+PW-22(8) = 81 points
- Low points: PW-12(5)+PW-18(13)+PW-19(8)+PW-23(5)+PW-24(8) = 39 points
Total points = 21+63+81+39 = 204 (rounding note: recompute gives 204 vs earlier 203; using 204 for breakdown consistency, negligible variance line item).

Blended rate per point (all-in, overhead included) = 1,918 hours * 75 / 204 points ≈ $705/point.
Urgent: 21 * 705 ≈ $14,805
High: 63 * 705 ≈ $44,415
Medium: 81 * 705 ≈ $57,105
Low: 39 * 705 ≈ $27,495
Sum ≈ $143,820 (rounding matches total within a few dollars of $143,850).

Non-labour costs: no infrastructure/tooling/license costs were specified in the brief. I've added a small indicative placeholder line for cloud/staging infra and Stripe fees setup, clearly flagged as an assumption/estimate since no vendor quotes were given.

Scenarios (P50/P80/P95) reflect uncertainty from: (a) single-role, single-FTE staffing making the schedule fragile to absence/illness, (b) unproven estimate-to-actual ratio absent historical actuals, (c) elevated technical risk in PW-7 (payments) and PW-8 (migration).

assumptions: The rate card provided is explicitly a PLACEHOLDER: a single generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE. No real roles (e.g. developer, QA, PM, DevOps) or differentiated rates have been assigned yet, so this entire estimate is indicative only and must be revisited once actual team roles and rates are set.

No historical actuals (real spend or velocity data) exist for this project; hours were derived from story points using an industry-typical heuristic (~7 build hours/point) plus overhead, not from proven team velocity.

Story points were converted to hours assuming a blended small-team effort of 7 hours per point for core build work, plus ~10% for coordination/PM overhead, ~15% for QA/regression, and ~10% contingency buffer, given the presence of high-risk items (payments, legacy migration, compliance).

With only 1 FTE available, the calculated ~1,918 hours implies roughly 11-12 months of continuous solo full-time work; this is a scheduling/capacity risk independent of the dollar total — the team is very likely understaffed for this backlog and timeline expectations should be adjusted or headcount increased.
All 24 backlog items are assumed in-scope for this estimate; no items have been descoped yet (see reductions for suggested descoping).
Non-labour costs (hosting, Stripe fees, migration tooling) are rough indicative placeholders since no vendor quotes or infrastructure sizing were supplied.
Priority-based cost breakdown allocates the same blended all-in hourly effort proportionally by story points within each priority band.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 Admin back-office for support staff (Low priority, 13 points) to a later phase; support staff can use existing DB tools temporarily.
reductions.effect: Removes ~13 points (~122 hours) of build effort from current scope.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 Usage analytics and reporting and PW-23 Contract tests against helpdesk API (Low priority, 8+5=13 points) to a post-launch phase.
reductions.effect: Removes 13 points of Low-priority scope not required for launch.

reductions.description: Simplify PW-14 Multi-currency support to launch with USD only, adding EUR/PLN in a later release, reducing points from 13 to an estimated 5.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~8 points of scope while preserving a functional single-currency launch.

reductions.description: Reduce QA/regression overhead allocation from 15% to 10% of core hours by adopting stronger automated test coverage from the start (shifts cost rather than eliminates risk).
reductions.effect: Lowers overhead hours by ~5% of the 1,421 core hours (~71 hours) at $75/hr.

reductions.description: Defer PW-24 Decommission the legacy portal until after the new portal has been live and stable for a full billing cycle, moving it out of this budget cycle.
reductions.effect: Removes 8 points of Low-priority work from the current cost estimate.
